senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; v. שׁוּק I) [meeting place,] market, street.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 91">Gen. R. s. 91</cite> <he>ש׳ של זונות</he> the place where harlots meet.
<cite ref="Pesachim 110a:3">Pes. 110ᵃ</cite> <he>בזמן שלא ראה פני הש׳</he> if he has not seen the open, i.e. if he has not been in the open air between one cup and the other.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 115a:12">B. Kam. 115ᵃ</cite> <he>תקנת הש׳</he> the market ordinance (that he who buys a stolen object publicly has a right to his purchasing money on restoring the object).
Yeb. 53ᵃ התרת יבמה לש׳ making a y’bamah permitted to all the world, i.e. freeing a woman from her dependence on her brother-in-law.
Ib. 98ᵇ פגע ביבמה לש׳ he might (on marrying her) strike on a ‘y’bamah abroad’, i.e. on one bound to another man as her yabam; a. v. fr.—

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 20">Num. R. s. 20<sup>18</sup></cite>, a. e. <he>בעל הש׳</he> market commissioner.—Pl. <cite ref="U00354"><he>שְׁוָוקִים</he></cite>, <cite ref="U00354"><he>שְׁוָוקִין</he></cite>, <he>שְׁוָקִ׳</he>.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 20">Ib</cite>.<sup>17</sup> (expl. <he>קרית חצות</he>, <cite ref="Numbers 22:39">Num. XXII, 39</cite>) <he>שעשה ש׳ של וכ׳</he> he arranged commercial markets.
<cite ref="Shabbat 33b:5">Sabb. 33ᵇ</cite> <he>תקנו ש׳ וכ׳</he> they (the Romans in Palestine) made markets to place harlots there; <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 2b:4">Ab. Zar. 2ᵇ</cite>.
<cite ref="Tosefta Makhshirin 3:8">Tosef. Makhsh. III, 8</cite> <he>הבאין מבית הש׳</he> that are brought back from the market houses; a. fr.—Constr. <he>שׁוּקֵי</he>.
<cite ref="Eruvin 29a">Erub. 29ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>הריני … בש׳ טבריא</he> I am (to-day) as bright as Ben ʿAzzai was in the meeting places of Tiberias; a. fr.
